history.heading: Vikings and the medieval kingdom
paragraphs: Norway, a long country along the western edge of Scandinavia, has been inhabited since the end of the last Ice Age. The Sámi people have lived in the north for thousands of years. In the Viking Age (around 800–1050), Norwegian seafarers raided, traded and settled across the North Atlantic, reaching Iceland, Greenland and North America.

Harald Fairhair is traditionally said to have unified Norway around 872. Christianity was established in the 11th century, and Olav II became the national saint. The medieval kingdom reached its height in the 13th century.

history.heading: Union with Denmark and Sweden
paragraphs: The Black Death in 1349 devastated Norway, and in 1380 it entered a union with Denmark that lasted over four centuries. In 1814 Denmark ceded Norway to Sweden, but Norwegians adopted their own constitution on 17 May 1814, now the national day, and entered a looser union with Sweden. Norway became fully independent in 1905 and chose a Danish prince as King Haakon VII.

history.heading: Modern Norway
paragraphs: Norway was neutral in the First World War but occupied by Nazi Germany from 1940 to 1945; collaborator Vidkun Quisling's name became a word for traitor. After the war Norway joined NATO in 1949 and built a comprehensive welfare state.

Oil was discovered in the North Sea in 1969, transforming the country into one of the world's richest. Norwegians rejected EU membership in referendums in 1972 and 1994. In 2011 a far-right terrorist killed 77 people in Oslo and on Utøya island.

culture.heading: Language and literature
paragraphs: Norwegian has two official written forms, Bokmål and Nynorsk, and many dialects; Sámi languages are also official in some areas. Most Norwegians belong to the Church of Norway, though few are active.

Norway has produced playwright Henrik Ibsen, composer Edvard Grieg, painter Edvard Munch (The Scream) and novelist Jon Fosse, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023. Fjords, such as Geirangerfjord, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

culture.heading: Outdoor life
paragraphs: Friluftsliv, the love of outdoor life, is central to Norwegian culture, and the right to roam allows free access to nature. Norway is the most successful nation in Winter Olympics history, especially in cross-country skiing and biathlon. Food includes salmon, cod, brown cheese (brunost) and lutefisk.

politics.heading: Constitutional monarchy
paragraphs: Norway is a constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy; King Harald V has reigned since 1991. The prime minister leads the government, responsible to the Storting (parliament), elected by proportional representation. The Labour Party is the largest party and won the 2025 election.
Norway is a NATO member but not in the EU; it belongs to the European Economic Area and Schengen. Oslo awards the Nobel Peace Prize, and Norway is known for peace mediation and generous foreign aid.

economy.heading: Oil wealth
paragraphs: Norway is one of the world's richest countries. Oil and gas from the North Sea and the Barents Sea are the largest exports, making Norway a key energy supplier to Europe. Revenues are placed in the Government Pension Fund Global, the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, worth well over a trillion US dollars.

Fishing and aquaculture, especially salmon farming, shipping and hydropower are also important; almost all electricity is renewable. Norway leads the world in electric car adoption. The currency is the Norwegian krone.
